subsystems.name: Light absorbers
subsystems.role: Capture sunlight and create the electron–hole pairs that drive the reactions.
parts: semiconductor thin films (e.g. silicon, metal oxides)
tandem or multijunction stacks to absorb more of the solar spectrum

subsystems.name: Catalysts
subsystems.role: Speed up CO2 reduction and water oxidation while steering the reaction toward useful products.

subsystems.name: Membrane and separator
subsystems.role: Keep the oxidation and reduction half-reactions apart while allowing ions to move between them.

subsystems.name: Reactor and electrolyte
subsystems.role: Contain the electrodes and manage the flow of water, CO2 and dissolved products.

subsystems.name: Product separation and upgrading
subsystems.role: Isolate and concentrate the chemicals formed, and convert them into fuels or food if needed.

buildSteps.title: Select and synthesize light absorbers
buildSteps.detail: Choose semiconductors with band gaps that absorb visible light, then deposit them as thin films on conductive substrates using techniques like chemical vapour deposition or sputtering.

buildSteps.title: Prepare catalysts
buildSteps.detail: Synthesize nanoparticles or molecular catalysts for CO2 reduction and water oxidation, and test their activity, selectivity and stability in small cells.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the membrane electrode assembly
buildSteps.detail: Coat the catalysts onto electrodes and sandwich them with an ion-conducting membrane so that the two half-reactions stay separate but ions can flow.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the reactor
buildSteps.detail: Stack the electrodes and membrane in a flow cell with inlets for CO2 and water and outlets for products, ensuring even flow and good electrical contact.

buildSteps.title: Test performance
buildSteps.detail: Measure solar-to-fuel efficiency, product yield and how long the device lasts under simulated sunlight, using gas chromatography and other analytical tools.

buildSteps.title: Improve stability and scale
buildSteps.detail: Develop protective coatings and more robust catalysts, then scale up electrode area from square centimetres to square metres while keeping performance uniform.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with CO2 sources
buildSteps.detail: Couple the device to a concentrated CO2 stream, such as flue gas from a cement or steel plant, and add product purification or upgrading steps.

buildSteps.title: Add biological steps for carbohydrates
buildSteps.detail: For the carbohydrate goal, feed simple products like formate or methanol to engineered enzymes or microbes that build sugars, linking artificial and biological catalysis.

prerequisites.why: Existing photovoltaics convert sunlight well, but absorbers optimised for direct solar-driven chemistry are still less efficient and stable.
Copper can make multi-carbon products, but selectivity and long-term stability remain poor.
Metal oxides work in the lab but tend to corrode or lose activity over time.
Membranes used in electrolysers and fuel cells can separate half-reactions, though they are not yet optimised for all products.
No established mass-production method exists for large-area devices that combine light absorbers, catalysts and membranes.

pathway.milestone: Lab-scale devices produce simple fuels such as carbon monoxide and formate from CO2 and sunlight at low efficiency.
pathway.unlocks: Proof that the basic chemistry can be driven by light.

pathway.milestone: Pilot modules run continuously for hundreds of hours with improved efficiency, targeting fuels for industry.
pathway.unlocks: Reliable operation and data for scale-up.

pathway.milestone: Integration with industrial CO2 sources and renewable hydrogen to make chemicals like methanol.
pathway.unlocks: A route to lower-carbon chemicals and fuels.

pathway.milestone: Hybrid artificial–biological systems convert simple products into carbohydrates for food.
pathway.unlocks: Food production that does not depend on farmland or weather.

pathway.milestone: Large-scale deployment for climate mitigation, if costs and stability improve.
pathway.unlocks: A supplementary path to capture and use CO2.
